::: {.why}
It is usually presented as a black box and it is a conjugate Bayesian update you could have derived yourself, which makes it the easiest place this week for your training to do real work.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the Black-Litterman posterior mean as a precision-weighted average of two sources, and name both.
- Show what happens to the optimised weights as the confidence in your views goes to zero and to infinity.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read the Black and Litterman paper as far as the statement of the combined estimator, then rederive the posterior yourself as a normal-normal update with the equilibrium returns as the prior mean and the views as noisy observations. It is the same algebra as combining two studies with different standard errors.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Implement it on your 25 assets, taking equilibrium returns by reverse-optimising from market weights, then adding one relative view. Plot the optimised weights as the view's confidence goes from near zero to near certainty, and confirm both limits are what you predicted.
:::
:::
